l-001.evidence: The squid access query (seq 0) returned row_count 48 over the operation window, while all three controls (C-21d, C-28d, C-35d), each with window_live: true, returned row_count 0 with empty values arrays. The observed rows carry distinguishing content in fields these queries surface — url.original values ifconfig.me:443, pastebin.com:443, transfer.sh:443, raw.githubusercontent.com:443, api.telegram.org:443, example.com:443, all with http.request.method CONNECT and squid.result_status TCP_TUNNEL/200 except transfer.sh which is consistently TCP_TUNNEL/503 with 0 bytes — none of which appear in any baseline. The distinction does not rest on source.ip (172.18.0.6), which environment_notes marks unstable; url.original, result_status and response bytes (~5.4–5.7KB, plus ~47.6KB per pastebin fetch) carry it, on a ~7-second beacon cadence from 07:06:11 to 07:06:46. Truncation of the payload at 40 of 48 rows does not affect this reading, since presence rather than absence is being established; seq 1 is unreadable and seq 2 is a cmdb entity record (state-only), neither of which contradicts seq 0.

l-002.evidence: Both queries in this lead are identity system lookups (`identity.access-check`, `identity.user-authorization`) returning an entity record and its authorization state, not an event stream. The observed payloads are a permission verdict (`authorized: true`, `via: override`, `role: developer`, `sudo: true`) and a user record (`username: dev.dana`, `enabled: true`, `realm_role: developer`, `authorized_hosts: [dev-ws-1, jump-box-1, office-ws-1]`, `sudo_hosts: [office-ws-1]`) — neither carries a `@timestamp` bound that a control window could move. The empty `baseline` is therefore expected and structural, not a measurement gap; `environment_notes.state_and_lookup_systems` names identity queries explicitly as `state-only`. Both queries agree, so the lead is not heterogeneous.
